title: Rate Lock Commitment Pricing of a New Lock After a Borrower Cancellation
content:
**Policy statement.** Locks on the same loan file are read together. A new Rate Lock Commitment requested on a loan file within the cooling period that started when the borrower cancelled an earlier lock on the same file is priced at worst case.

**Counting the cooling period.** Count calendar days forward from the cancelled lock's closed date, which is day zero. A request dated on the last day of the period is still inside it. The length of the cooling period is the product's cooling period after a borrower cancellation, as set in the product's cancellation cooling terms.

**Worst case.** Worst case means the higher of two prices: the cancelled lock's locked price at its locked rate, and the current rate-sheet price for that rate plus the new term's adjustment.

**Outside the rule.** Locks cancelled by the system because the file was withdrawn, denied or closed do not start a cooling period. A lock on a different loan file is never affected.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical, with a 30-day cooling period)

| Earlier lock on the same file | New request dated | Within the cooling period |
|---|---|---|
| Cancelled by the borrower; closed date is day zero | Day 30 | Yes, priced at worst case |
| Cancelled by the borrower; closed date is day zero | Day 31 | No |
| Cancelled by the system after the file was withdrawn | Any day | No cooling period started |
| Cancelled by the borrower, on another loan file | Any day | Not affected |

### Worked illustration (hypothetical figures)

The cancelled lock carried 0.500 points at its locked rate. Today's rate-sheet price for that rate is 0.250 points, and the new term's adjustment is 0.125 points, giving 0.375 points. The higher of 0.500 and 0.375 is 0.500 points, so the new lock is priced at 0.500 points.
